editorial.headline: Private Heritage Stewardship: Open Nationally, Closed to PMA in Bali
editorial.standfirst: Private stewardship of heritage places is open across all business scales nationally, but Bali’s permanent PMA moratorium prevents foreign-owned registration at a Bali address.
editorial.body:
At its heart, this is a stewardship activity. It covers private operation and preservation of places whose significance lies in history, science, education, religion, or culture: human-shaped landscapes and gardens, buildings, and heritage sites, whether built cultural heritage or natural heritage. Temples, saints’ tombs, and historic mosques are named examples, but the principle is broader: keeping a meaningful place operating and cared for. It also embraces historic sites and buildings, and archaeological sites that visitors can enter. The emphasis is the continuing life and preservation of the site, not simply the existence of an old structure.

That distinction matters in practice. The code is for private operators entrusted with a site’s ongoing operation and preservation. It does not extend to the construction-side work of renovating or restoring historical places, to architectural rehabilitation or restoration work, to archaeological excavation, or to the restoration and preventive conservation of museum artworks and collections performed outside a unit of this type. In other words, it describes the private steward of a heritage place and of visitor access to an archaeological site; it is not a catch-all label for every specialist intervention that may occur around heritage.

The national investment position is unambiguous: the activity is TERBUKA, with foreign ownership permitted up to 100%. Registration is stated to be available for Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar enterprises, so the classification is not reserved for a particular business scale. Those national facts make this a clear route for a private heritage operator outside the Bali-specific constraint. They do not, however, translate automatically into a Bali registration for a foreign-owned company.

On a Bali address, the position is closed today for PMA registration. The record identifies the Besar scale as Menengah Rendah and says that this triggers Bali’s PMA moratorium, which blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk activities island-wide on a permanent basis. The cited Governor’s letter dates from May 2026. The result must be stated plainly: a foreigner cannot register this activity in Bali today, notwithstanding the national 100% foreign-ownership ceiling. The national permission is real; Bali’s local PMA bar is equally real.
